set.hook: A Nordic-trained tasting kitchen in a glass box on the fifth floor of the Greek National Opera.
set.why: The restaurant takes its name from the old Faliro delta, the marshy mouth of the Kifissos that Renzo Piano's park and opera house now cover. Booking runs through Tock with a 100-euro deposit, and each seating is capped at three hours. In late 2025 La Liste named it Greece's top restaurant for 2026.

set.hook: Thissio's classic lamb-chop grill: two branches on a rail-side lane, chops by the kilo, barrel wine.
set.why: Athens calls places like this paidakia joints, and Atlas Obscura names To Steki tou Ilia the classic of the type. set.hook: A Cappadocian-refugee deli and meze room by Varvakios market, built around pastourma and soutzouki.
set.why: The Karamanlides were Turkish-speaking Orthodox Christians from Cappadocia who printed books in Turkish using the Greek alphabet, and many reached Greece in the 1923 exchange. Fanis Theodoropoulos, from a family of charcutiers on Evripidou, turned their cured-meat tradition into a deli with tables in 2014. One side is a counter of pastourma, soutzouki and cheeses; the other serves meze built from them. Vacuum-packed cuts travel well.

set.hook: The 1922 Armenian pastourma shop on Evripidou: cured beef by weight, with a small tasting corner.
set.why: In 1922 Miran Kourounlian, an Armenian refugee from Caesarea in Cappadocia, began curing beef into pastourma in Piraeus; a few years later he opened a narrow shop at Evripidou 45. His grandsons Miran and Krikor run it today. A renovation gave the old counter a facade of living plants, and inside a tasting corner serves the house pastourma, soutzouki and cured beef in the middle of the spice street's trade.

set.hook: A Politiki-cooking cafe aman in Nea Chalkidona, with live songs late in the week and Sunday family lunches.
set.why: Nea Chalkidona took its name from Chalcedon, on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, when refugees from Constantinople settled it after 1922, and Peran is named for Pera across the water. Meze come round on a tray to choose from, the bread and syrup sweets are made in house, and Sunday afternoon is for long family lunches.

set.hook: An Ano Petralona mageireio from 1930, opposite the Zefyros open-air cinema, where the day's pots run out.
set.why: The Oikonomou family opened a butcher's with a cooking pot on the corner of Troon and Kydantidon in 1930, and the son, Nikos, took it over in 1950. Finish with the orange pie with ice cream, then cross to Zefyros.

set.hook: An Exarcheia room cooking only on wood and charcoal, with Greek village recipes and 400 mostly natural wines.
set.why: Pharaoh opened on Solomou as a partnership between Cretan chef Manolis Papoutsakis, food journalist Fotis Vallatos, baritone Dimitris Platanias and wine man Perry Panagiotakopoulos. Look for the dolmadakia with xygalo, the tarama under bottarga and a galaktoboureko with its own following.
